# Validating a signed token (verifyClick)

> Verifies a signed click token by recomputing its HMAC-SHA256 signature in constant time and rejecting it if expired.

_Part of [Signed click token with 30-minute expiry](click-token.md)_

A click token pairs a base64url-encoded claims object with a truncated HMAC-SHA256 signature in the format `payload.mac`, created by [Creating a signed token (signClick)](sign-click.md). [`verifyClick`](ad-click-tracking-and-fraud.md) recomputes the HMAC signature from the payload, verifies it matches the received signature in constant time, decodes the claims from base64url JSON, and checks that the expiry time `e` is in the future. Any validation failure returns `null`. In [Ad click tokens and fraud checks](ad-click-tracking-and-fraud.md), [`verifyClick`](ad-click-tracking-and-fraud.md) ensures that a click token is legitimate and not stale. Ads can only be charged for impressions within 30 minutes of being shown, so expired or forged tokens are rejected before the click is tracked or billed.

**Look at:** [`verifyClick` in click-token.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/marketing/domain/click-token.ts#L22)

## Pieces

- Constant-time HMAC signature comparison prevents timing attacks: `timingSafeEqual` compares the computed and received signatures in fixed time, regardless of match, so attackers cannot use timing differences to forge valid signatures.

## What it touches

| Kind | Name | How |
|---|---|---|
| other | `Click token (payload.mac format)` | Base64url-encoded JSON claims followed by a dot and a truncated HMAC-SHA256 signature (first 32 base64url characters). |

## Watch out

- The HMAC signature is truncated to 32 base64url characters, not the full 64-character SHA256 digest.
- Any validation failure returns `null`—callers cannot distinguish between a bad signature, malformed token, or expired token.
- Expiry time `e` in claims is in milliseconds; comparing to seconds will reject all tokens.
- `JSON.parse` on invalid payload JSON throws an error instead of returning null; if the JSON is valid but missing required fields, the function returns incomplete claims without validating.
